simple.meaning: תָּלָא (tâlâʼ) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to suspend ; figuratively (through hesitation) to be uncertain ; by implication (of mental dependence) to habituate.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 2 times in Deuteronomy, Hosea, beginning at Deuteronomy 28:66. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to תָּלָא (H8511) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: תָּלָא (tâlâʼ) / H8511 is traced through Deuteronomy 28:66, Hosea 11:7 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to suspend ; figuratively (through hesitation) to be uncertain ; by implication (of mental dependence) to habituate
definitions.full: H8511. tala תָּלָא verb hang (|| form of תלה , Ges § 75rr ); — Qal Perfect 3plural suffix תְּלָאוּם 2Sam 21:12 Qr the Philistines had hanged them (Kt תלום ; see Dr); Passive participle תְּלֻאִים Deut 28:66 thy life shall be hung up before thee, i.e. be in suspense, each moment uncertain. — לִמְשׁוּבָתִי תְלוּאִים וְעַמִּי Hosea 11:7 my people is hung up to my backsliding is certainly corrupt (AV bent to backsliding from me , i.e. huge or swung toward turning from me, compare GASm, but very dubious); Marti conjectures אֶלעֲֿצַבִּים נִלְוִים ; Oettli Now 2Harper נִלְאָה or הֶלְאַ֫נִי has wearied itself [ me ] in backsliding. [ תַּלְאֻבָה ] see לאב . תְּלָאָה see לאה .
